intro: Searching for an equity release broker near you usually means you're thinking about releasing money tied up in your home and want someone local who can talk it through face to face. You may be weighing up whether it's the right step at all, or you may already know you want to go ahead and need help comparing what's out there. Either way, the decision deserves careful thought and proper regulated advice.
need_heading: What people searching for a local equity release broker usually need
need_lead: Most people looking for a broker near them want clear, unhurried help understanding whether equity release suits their circumstances.
needs: You own your home and are considering releasing some of its value to top up your retirement income.
You want to compare plans from across the market rather than being shown a single lender's product.
You need someone to explain the difference between lump sum and drawdown arrangements in plain terms.
You would like to understand how voluntary repayments work and what they could mean for the amount owed over time.
You want a local professional you can sit down with, and you'd like to involve your family in the conversation.
context_heading: Why whole-of-market access and features matter here
context: Equity release brokers compare plans across lenders and features such as drawdown and voluntary repayments, so it's worth asking whether the adviser can look at the whole market rather than a limited panel. Plans differ in how the money is released, how interest is treated and what flexibility you have to repay, so the detail really does matter.

Equity release advice is regulated by the FCA, and advisers must hold a specialist qualification. You can check the firm on the FCA register, and it's worth asking whether it is a member of the Equity Release Council, whose standards include protection against negative equity and the right to stay in your home for life. You will also need your own solicitor to explain the legal documents before you sign.
tell_heading: What to tell iComply when you enquire
tell: Mention that you're looking for an equity release broker near you and say which town or area you'd like them to cover.
Explain whether you're after a lump sum, a drawdown arrangement or simply want to explore the options.
Say roughly what you'd like the released money for, such as topping up income or covering a specific cost.
Mention whether anyone else owns or lives in the property, as this affects the advice.
Say whether you'd like to involve family members in discussions with the adviser.
Note any preferences about meeting in person, by phone or at home, so we can introduce someone who works that way.
questions_heading: Questions to ask the equity release adviser
questions: Can you confirm you advise across the whole market rather than a limited panel of lenders?
How do drawdown and lump sum plans differ, and which might suit my circumstances?
What flexibility would I have to make voluntary repayments, and how would that affect what I owe?
How are your fees structured, and when would I need to pay them?
Are you a member of the Equity Release Council, and what do its standards mean for me?
How will you help me involve my family and my own solicitor in the process?

faqs.q: Do I need a solicitor as well as an equity release adviser?
faqs.a: Yes. You will need your own solicitor to explain the legal documents before you sign, separately from the adviser who arranges the plan. Many advisers encourage you to involve family members in the discussion too.

faqs.q: How can I check that an equity release adviser is properly regulated?
faqs.a: Equity release advice is regulated by the FCA, and advisers must hold a specialist qualification. You can check the firm on the FCA register before you go ahead, and it's worth asking whether it is a member of the Equity Release Council.

faqs.q: What does whole-of-market mean when choosing a broker?
faqs.a: It means the adviser can compare plans across lenders rather than only offering products from a limited panel. Because features such as drawdown and voluntary repayments vary between plans, whole-of-market access matters when you're weighing up your options.

faqs.q: Will I be told about fees before I commit?
faqs.a: Fees must be explained to you, so ask how the adviser charges and when payment would fall due. Quotes are on application, so it's sensible to get this clear early in the conversation.
